pois.title: Bodhidharma

metadata.label: Medium / Technique
metadata.value: Ink and colors on paper, Hanging scroll

pois.content:
This is a representative work by Hakuin Ekaku depicting Bodhidharma. Bodhidharma was an Indian monk who journeyed to China and became the founder of Zen Buddhism. In the upper left of the painting, there is an inscription created with the wax-resist technique: after writing the characters with wax, Hakuin applied dark ink, causing only the wax-protected letters to stand out white against the inked background. The inscription reads, "Directly point to the human mind; see one's true nature and attain Buddhahood." In other words: "Gaze honestly at your own mind; awaken to the Buddha-nature originally inherent within yourself." This represents the essence of Zen teaching as Bodhidharma preached. Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769), revered as the great revitalizer of the Rinzai sect during the mid-Edo period, created countless paintings to communicate Zen's teachings in accessible ways.

![Detail of Bodhidharma](https://res.cloudinary.com/dui2mxeuh/image/upload/v1764338529/large_51_100692_20200722_LA_588_002_L_144e34dcbd.jpg)
